views.name: engagements_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  EngagementNumber,
  StartDate,
  EndDate,
  StartTime,
  StopTime,
  ContractPrice,
  CustomerID,
  AgentID,
  EntertainerID,
  -- derived: number of days for multi-day engagements (integer, 0 when same day or null inputs)
  CASE
    WHEN StartDate IS NOT NULL AND EndDate IS NOT NULL THEN julianday(EndDate) - julianday(StartDate)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_days,
  -- derived: seconds between StartTime and StopTime on the same day when both times present
  CASE
    WHEN StartTime IS NOT NULL AND StopTime IS NOT NULL THEN
      (strftime('%s', '2000-01-01 ' || StopTime) - strftime('%s', '2000-01-01 ' || StartTime))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_seconds
FROM Engagements
views.description: Normalized engagement rows: canonical pass-through of Engagements with explicit derived duration_days and duration_seconds measures (when both StartDate/EndDate or StartTime/StopTime present). Useful as a clean engagement fact for downstream joins, aggregations, and time-based filters. | Use for: Compute total revenue by month/week/day from engagements; Filter engagements by duration or time-of-day; Join engagements to customers/agents/entertainers for reporting

views.name: engagements_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EngagementNumber,
  e.StartDate,
  e.EndDate,
  e.StartTime,
  e.StopTime,
  e.ContractPrice,
  e.CustomerID,
  c.CustFirstName,
  c.CustLastName,
  c.CustCity,
  c.CustState,
  e.AgentID,
  a.AgtFirstName,
  a.AgtLastName,
  a.AgtCity,
  a.Salary,
  e.EntertainerID,
  ent.EntStageName,
  ent.EntCity,
  ent.EntWebPage
FROM Engagements e
LEFT JOIN Customers c ON e.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
LEFT JOIN Agents a ON e.AgentID = a.AgentID
LEFT JOIN Entertainers ent ON e.EntertainerID = ent.EntertainerID
views.description: Denormalized engagements enriched with customer, agent and entertainer attributes. Preserves all keys for safe downstream joins and exposes commonly used descriptive columns for reporting and grouping. | Use for: Reports listing engagements with customer/agent/entertainer details; Aggregate revenue by agent/entertainer/customer location; Filter engagements by customer city or entertainer name

views.name: agent_engagements_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AgentID,
  COUNT(EngagementNumber) AS engagement_count,
  SUM(ContractPrice) AS total_contract_price,
  AVG(ContractPrice) AS avg_contract_price,
  MIN(StartDate) AS first_engagement_date,
  MAX(StartDate) AS last_engagement_date
FROM Engagements
GROUP BY AgentID
views.description: Aggregated engagement measures per AgentID: counts, total and average ContractPrice, first and last engagement dates. Useful for performance/ranking of agents and time series rollups. | Use for: Who are the top-performing agents by revenue or bookings?; Time-bounded aggregations when combined with a filtered engagements_base CTE; Average contract price per agent

views.name: entertainer_style_strengths
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  EntertainerID,
  StyleID,
  COUNT(*) AS style_row_count,
  AVG(StyleStrength) AS avg_style_strength,
  MIN(StyleStrength) AS min_style_strength,
  MAX(StyleStrength) AS max_style_strength
FROM Entertainer_Styles
GROUP BY EntertainerID, StyleID
views.description: Aggregate style strength per EntertainerID and StyleID with counts and average StyleStrength. Useful for profiling entertainer skillsets and matching to customer preferences. | Use for: Find entertainers strongest in a given style; Match entertainers to customer preferred styles; Summarize style coverage across entertainers

views.name: customer_style_preferences
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mp.CustomerID,
  mp.StyleID,
  mp.PreferenceSeq,
  ms.StyleName,
  c.CustFirstName,
  c.CustLastName,
  c.CustCity,
  c.CustState
FROM Musical_Preferences mp
LEFT JOIN Musical_Styles ms ON mp.StyleID = ms.StyleID
LEFT JOIN Customers c ON mp.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
views.description: Customer preferences joined to style names and preference sequence. Use to match customers to entertainers or to segment customers by preferred musical styles. | Use for: List customers who prefer a particular style; Rank entertainers that match top customer preferences; Segment customers by top preference sequence

views.name: entertainer_member_roster
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  em.EntertainerID,
  em.MemberID,
  em.Status,
  m.MbrFirstName,
  m.MbrLastName,
  m.MbrPhoneNumber,
  m.Gender
FROM Entertainer_Members em
LEFT JOIN Members m ON em.MemberID = m.MemberID
views.description: Roster of members for each entertainer with member contact and status. Useful for investigating group composition or contacting individual members. | Use for: Which members belong to an entertainer and their contact info?; Filter active/inactive members for an entertainer; Aggregate member counts per entertainer

views.name: agent_hire_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AgentID,
  AgtFirstName,
  AgtLastName,
  DateHired,
  Salary,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY DateHired ASC, AgentID ASC) AS agent_hire_rank
FROM Agents
views.description: Rank agents by DateHired (earliest hire = rank 1). Exposes agent_hire_rank for use in Top-K queries or tenure-based filters. | Use for: Find earliest-hired agents or top-k most tenured; Combine with engagement aggregates to compare tenure vs performance

views.name: entertainer_recent_engagement_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EngagementNumber,
  e.EntertainerID,
  e.StartDate,
  e.ContractPrice,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.EntertainerID ORDER BY e.StartDate DESC, e.EngagementNumber DESC) AS engagement_rank
FROM Engagements e
views.description: For each entertainer, rank engagements by StartDate descending so downstream queries can pick the most recent engagement(s) per entertainer using agent WHERE engagement_rank = 1 or <=K. | Use for: Find the latest engagement per entertainer; Get top-K recent engagements per entertainer

views.name: monthly_engagements_calendar
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EngagementNumber,
  e.StartDate,
  e.ContractPrice,
  zm.YearNumber,
  zm.MonthNumber,
  zm.MonthYear,
  zm.MonthStart,
  zm.MonthEnd
FROM Engagements e
LEFT JOIN ztblMonths zm ON DATE(e.StartDate) BETWEEN DATE(zm.MonthStart) AND DATE(zm.MonthEnd)
views.description: Join engagements to ztblMonths via StartDate to enable month-level reporting. Exposes MonthStart/MonthEnd and YearNumber/MonthNumber for grouping by calendar month. | Use for: Aggregate revenue by calendar month; Filter engagements falling into a particular month/year

views.name: entertainer_style_match_score
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  es.EntertainerID,
  es.StyleID,
  es.StyleStrength,
  -- normalized strength per style (0..1)
  CASE
    WHEN max_strength.max_style_strength IS NULL OR max_strength.max_style_strength = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(es.StyleStrength AS REAL) / max_strength.max_style_strength
  END AS style_strength_norm
FROM Entertainer_Styles es
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT StyleID, MAX(StyleStrength) AS max_style_strength
  FROM Entertainer_Styles
  GROUP BY StyleID
) AS max_strength ON es.StyleID = max_strength.StyleID
views.description: Calculated per entertainer/style a simple normalized strength score between 0 and 1 based on StyleStrength relative to max observed in that style. Useful for matching entertainers to customer preferences as a normalized measure. | Use for: Normalize stylistic strengths for cross-style matching; Rank entertainers for a style using normalized scores
